_about: THE REFUSAL CONTRACT, MEASURED FROM THE REAL HOST, ASSERTED FROM BOTH SIDES.
smb_funnel/README.md claims the funnel 'speaks the real host contract either way'.
It did not: smb_host is FastAPI and answers {detail: ...}, while src/mock_core.js
answered {error: ...} with different statuses — and the mock PROVISIONED two
inputs the host refuses outright (a punctuation-only name, a non-string name),
so the demo backend showed a success path the product does not have.
This file is the single statement of what a refusal looks like. Two suites read
it and neither can drift without the other going red:
smb_host/test_main.py            drives the REAL host against it
smb_funnel/tests/contract-parity.test.mjs  drives the MOCK against it
If the host changes, its test reddens; updating this file then reddens the
mock's until the mock follows. A one-sided pin is what let them diverge.
detail is 'string' (an exact message both must produce) or 'array' (FastAPI's
validation list, where loc and type are pinned and msg wording is the
framework's to change).
Editing this file must wake BOTH suites. The CI 'changes' filter names it
explicitly for the smb_host job, which no Python path would otherwise match —
a filter that wakes only one side is a one-sided pin with extra steps.

provision.case: punctuation only — cannot slug to an id
provision.message: business_name must contain at least one alphanumeric character
business_name must contain at least one alphanumeric character
a business is already provisioned under the name 'Fadeaway Barbershop'

provision.case: contact names no channel a booking can be delivered on
provision.message: 'call me maybe' is neither an https webhook URL nor an email address, so it names no channel a booking can be delivered on
a plain http webhook is refused: a booking carries a customer's name and time, so the delivery URL must be https

book.message: missing required field(s): service, provider, datetime

_about: THE SUCCESS PATH, NOT ONLY THE REFUSALS.
Everything above states what a REFUSAL looks like. This states the one
value on the success path that both sides must agree on, and it is here
for the same reason: `booking.status` is asserted by smb_host's suite and
constructed by smb_funnel's mock, and until now each side held its own
copy of the literal. Two copies of a wire value with no shared statement
is how the mock became more permissive than the host on the refusal
path — the divergence this file was created to end.
THE VALUE IS `recorded`, NOT `confirmed`, AND THE WORD IS THE POINT.
The host writes a booking row and checks the slot was free. There is no
acceptance step anywhere in the path: nobody at the business agrees to
anything, and `status` is set before delivery is even consulted, so it
ships alongside `delivered: false` in the same response. `confirmed`
told a reader the business had agreed. `recorded` says what happened.
⚠️ THIS IS THE BOOKING'S STATUS, NOT AN HTTP STATUS. The `status` key
inside the refusal entries above is the HTTP code; this one is a field
of the response body. They are named apart on purpose.
⚠️ AND IT IS NOT THE BADGE VOCABULARY. `Signature valid - issuer not
confirmed` is the receipt-verification badge and has nothing to do with
a booking's status. A rename that swept the word `confirmed` across the
funnel would eat a load-bearing, separately-pinned label.
